answer.summary: ChatGPT's 56-row table (50 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands) gives every row at least one qualification checked against an official constitution, statute, court or election authority, with its link and the legal date it is tested on (filing, election or taking office, per row). UNKNOWN means not established, never eligible or ineligible. Rule-changing differences from the 2023 CSG survey: Kansas sets age 25 and qualified elector; Kentucky requires six years of state citizenship and residence (not two); Michigan four years as a registered elector; Maryland five years' residence and registered voter; Louisiana tests at qualification and establishes no standalone five-year residence; West Virginia tests age at the start of the term; California's five-year residence clause is unenforceable per its Secretary of State; South Carolina's religious test is judicially invalid and must not become a requirement. The owner's chosen display is a brief rule on each race listing with detail on request, and a rejection names the requirement and its date in election-office language.
